properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 22 at 5:50AM MST until October 22 at 6:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 550 AM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 6 miles northwest of
Cedar Creek, or 18 miles northwest of Whiteriver, moving northeast at
45 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Cedar Creek, Carrizo and White Mountain Apache Reservation.

This includes the following highways...
Highway 60 between mile markers 310 and 324. State Route 73 between
mile markers 311 and 322.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Torrential rainfall is also occurring with this storm and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.areaDesc: Garfield, UT; Kane, UT; San Juan, UT
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 6:16AM MDT until October 22 at 12:15PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...San Juan County in southeastern Utah...
Southwestern Garfield County in southern Utah...
Kane County in southern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of normally dry washes, slot canyons, rivers,
creeks, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations is occurring.
Prolonged and widespread moderate to heavy rainfall will continue
trough this evening. This coupled with near-saturated soils will
allow rapidly increasing flows across all waterways within the
warned area, including all of the Glen Canyon National Recreation
Area. Increasingly high flows are expected in, but not limited
to...the Paria River, Wahweep Creek, Warm Creek, Last Chance Creek,
Croton Canyon, and the Escalante River Basin and tributaries. Many
backcountry roads within this area are expected to become
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 610 AM MDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen across the headwaters of the
Paria River, Escalante River, Wahweap Creek and other drainages
within the warned area. The Paria River at Highway 89 saw a peak
flow of nearly 2500 CFS overnight, while the Escalante River just
downstream from Escalante recorded a peak stage of 6 feet. These
flood waves will continue to move downstream through the morning
hours.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2.5 inches are possible
through this evening. This will result in continued high flows
and additional flooding of all rivers, streams and normally dry
washes within the warned area.
- Glen Canyon National Recreation Area, including the Escalante
region. Kodachrome State Park, Tropic, Cannonville, Escalante,
and Big Water
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks can become unstable and
unsafe.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 21 at 9:21PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end of this
week. There is potential for levels to approach Major Flood Stage
next week after northeast winds increase again.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Wednesday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.2 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday morning at 1130 AM EDT.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 22 at 1:56AM MST until October 22 at 2:00PM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected along
Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River.

* WHERE...Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River from Cameron to
the Colorado River confluence.

* WHEN...Until 200 PM MST /300 PM MDT/ Tonight.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Moenkopi Wash and the Little Colorado River
is occurring. Further rises in the water levels of already flooded
creeks and normally dry washes. Deadly flooding over low-water
crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 152 AM MST /252 AM MDT/, Water levels in Moenkopi Wash
remained above major flood stage. Elevated flow was also observed
on the Little Colorado River near Cameron. With additional heavy
rain expected, flooding is expected to continue.
- This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Hamblin Wash, Begashibito Wash, Little Colorado River, Moenkopi
Wash, Bekihatso Wash, Fivemile Wash and Sheep Wash.

Flooding is occurring along Moenkopi Wash.
- For Moenkopi Wash near Tuba City:
At 12:45am MST /1:45am MDT/ the stage was 33.55 feet.
Flood Stage is 27.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 27.0 feet: At 27.0 feet water begins to encroach on homes in
lower Moenkopi Village and floods crop fields along the river.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tuba City, Moenkopi, Little Colorado River Navajo Tribal Park and
Salt Trail Canyon.
- This includes the following recreation areas andcampgrounds...
Blue Water Base Camp and Old Fish Camp Site.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 5:48AM MST until October 22 at 8:00AM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
At 548 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain over the Sycamore Burn Scar. Up to 0.75 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Sycamore Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Sycamore Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Gila County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Sycamore Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be
anticipated across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in
places. If you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

NWSheadline: FLASH FLOOD WARNING FOR THE SYCAMORE BURN SCAR REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 8 AM MST THIS MORNING FOR GILA COUNTY

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 22 at 2:32AM MST until October 22 at 8:15AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
At 332 AM MDT, a river gauge on Chine Creek within Canyon de Chelly
National Monument reported water levels had fallen below flood stage.
However, flooding will remain a threat in areas downstream of Canyon
de Chelly through the morning hours. Flash flooding is already
occurring.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding.

SOURCE...River gauge reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of Chine Creek.

For Chinle Creek at Chinle:
At 3:00am the stage was 3.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 4.0 feet.
Impacts:
At 3.6 feet: Chinle Creek becomes impassable to recreational
vehicles.
At 4.0 feet: Water begins to encroach upon structures just upstream
of the Highway 64 bridge near the Canyon de Chelly welcome center.
At 4.3 feet: Flooding to homes and residences in Chinle on left bank
downstream from Highway 64 bridge.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Chinle, Canyon De Chelly National Monument and Mummy Cave Overlook.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Junction Overlook, White House Overlook, Antelope House Overlook and
Face Rock Overlook.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Chinle Wash, Coyote Wash, Muerto, Canyon del, Sheep Dip Creek,
Black Rock Canyon and Nazlini Wash.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Stay away or be swept away! The banks of creeks and washes are
unstable and unsafe during any flooding event.
